sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that Yehudah represents the aspect of gratitude (hoda'ah) within the souls of Israel, which is revealed through his brothers Reuven, Shimon, and Levi, corresponding to the two sections of Shema and Emes Veyatziv, leading to the nullification of Shemoneh Esrei.

translations.translation: "Yehudah, you [shall be] praised by your brothers, etc."
And it is explained by the Alter Rebbe in Torah Or at the beginning of our portion,
that Yehudah is named for "this time I will thank (odeh) Hashem"
[and] it is the aspect of gratitude (hoda'ah) inherent in the collective souls of Israel.
And in order for this gratitude to be in a state of revelation, it is through "your brothers,"
Reuven, Shimon, and Levi
[the brothers of Yehudah who were born before him].
And this is "your brothers will praise you (yoducha),"
that "your brothers"
[Reuven, Shimon, and Levi]
are the ones who cause and bring about the aspect of gratitude (hoda'ah) of Yehudah
(so that it will be in revelation).
And it is explained there,
that Reuven and Shimon are the two sections of Kriyas Shema, and Levi is the aspect of Emes Veyatziv
(which follows Kriyas Shema),
and through this one subsequently comes to Shemoneh Esrei,
[which is] the aspect of gratitude (hoda'ah) and self-nullification (bittul) of the aspect of Yehudah.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that Reuven corresponds to the level of "seeing" in divine service, bringing about absolute certainty and love of Hashem, which is the first portion of Shema.

translations.translation: And the concept is
(as explained in Torah Or there),
that behold, Reuven is named for "because He saw (ra'ah) etc.,"
Shimon is named for "because He heard (shama) etc."
And their significance in the service of G-d
(in each and every Jew),
the aspect of Reuven is that his service to his Master is not only in the category of intellectual comprehension, but rather in the category of sight.
That is, his certainty in Divinity is with the greatest possible certainty,
analogous to a person who sees some thing, regarding whom it is impossible that he should have any doubt about it,
since he himself saw the thing.
And likewise is it in the service of G-d,
that his contemplation
[and particularly regarding the matter of Divine Providence]
is in a manner
(of seeing)
that the matter becomes certain for him as if he sees it with actual physical sight.
And from this sight he comes to the aspect of love of Hashem,
and as it is written
(regarding the naming of Reuven)
"because He saw... for now my husband will love me."
And this is the matter of the first portion of Kriyas Shema,
"And you shall love Hashem your G-d, etc."

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that Shimon corresponds to the level of "hearing" in divine service, which is a more distant level that leads to the service of fear, corresponding to the second portion of Shema.

translations.translation: And the aspect of Shimon
(named for "because He heard etc.")
is that his service is in the category of hearing and intellectual comprehension alone, and not in the category of sight.
And since he is then still in a state of distance
[analogous to a person who hears something that is told to him,
but he himself did not see],
therefore his service is in the line of fear.
And this is the matter of the second portion of Kriyas Shema,
"And it will be, if you surely listen... guard yourselves, lest your heart be seduced, etc."
For since the matter of Divinity is for him only in the category of hearing
("if you surely listen"),
therefore his service must be in the line of fear
("guard yourselves, etc.").
